label: USE CASE 16
title: How Ride Apps Set ETA and Surge Pricing

scenes.text: Why your cab costs more in rain. It's raining, it's 6 PM, and your cab app says, fares are higher than usual. [1] So why does the price jump, and how does it know the driver will arrive in 4 minutes? [2] Let's break down ride apps.

title: Surge
Pricing
data.subtitle: How ride apps set ETA and price
data.hook: Why your cab costs more *in rain*

scenes.text: When you book a ride, a lot happens in seconds. [1] You enter your pickup and destination. [2] The system finds nearby drivers, and predicts each one's arrival time. [3] It matches you with the best driver, not always the closest. [4] It predicts the trip time, using traffic and routes, [5] and then shows you the price.

The price part is called dynamic pricing, or surge. [1] When many people want rides, and few drivers are free, prices rise. [2] Demand goes up, like in rain or office hours, [3] supply is low, with few free drivers, [4] so the price multiplier rises, and more drivers head to that area.

data.definition: Prices that rise and fall with demand and the number of free drivers.

scenes.text: AI also predicts demand before it happens. [1] It learns patterns, like office rush hours, and flights landing at the airport. [2] It watches signals, like weather, events and festivals. [3] And it nudges drivers towards areas that will soon be busy.

So why do apps use surge at all? [1] With fixed prices, when demand spikes, there are simply no cars, and very long waits. [2] With dynamic prices, more drivers come online, so you can at least get a ride, but at a higher price.

left.title: Fixed price
left.label: but no cars when it's busy

scenes.text: Here are four terms. [1] ETA, the estimated time of arrival. [2] Matching, pairing riders with drivers. [3] The surge multiplier, how much higher than normal the fare is. [4] And forecasting, predicting future demand.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think surge prices are completely random. [2] They're mainly driven by demand and supply in your area, at that moment. So waiting a few minutes, or walking a little way, can often lower the price.

data.fact: They're mainly driven by demand and supply in your area right now.
data.tip: Wait a bit or walk a little

scenes.text: Quick quiz! Why do ride prices surge? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] High demand, and few free drivers!

options: High demand and few free drivers

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] The app matches you with the best driver, not just the closest. [2] It predicts arrival and trip times using traffic. [3] Surge comes from high demand and low supply.
